evidence.content: The measured ~2s wall-clock increase this week (14.59s at bbbaf4a -> 16.55s at HEAD, +14%) is explained by two newly landed subprocess-heavy end-to-end test files — test/runtime-evidence-write.test.js (new, 28 tests, ~7.9s standalone) and expanded test/install-shapes.test.js (~7.6s standalone) — landing alongside the pre-existing test/cli-e2e.test.js (~13s standalone, 46 tests, unchanged in this window). All three are dominated by real `node <cli/runtime>` subprocess spawns plus real filesystem I/O (installing/updating/rolling back skill trees across now 7 harnesses), not by algorithmic complexity in the test bodies. Because node --test parallelizes file execution across a limited pool (10 CPUs on this machine) and the other ~56 files each finish in well under 500ms, adding a third multi-second-per-file cost extends the run's critical path even though most files are fast; the suite's overall floor is effectively set by whichever of these three heaviest files finishes last, not by their sum.
